skills.name: The structure of the atom: Bohr's model

note.text:
In Bohr's model, electrons move around the nucleus in fixed shells (energy levels).
For the first 20 elements, fill the shells in order: the first shell holds up to 2 electrons, the second up to 8, the third up to 8, then the fourth.
Electron arrangement (configuration): sodium, 11 electrons: 2, 8, 1. Chlorine, 17: 2, 8, 7. Calcium, 20: 2, 8, 8, 2.
The electrons in the outer shell decide how an element reacts.
Draw the model: the nucleus in the middle, a circle for each shell, and dots or crosses for the electrons.

worked_example.problem: Write the electron arrangement of aluminium (atomic number {z}) and draw its Bohr model.
steps: {z} electrons. First shell: {2}. Second shell: {8}. That uses {10}.
The third shell gets the rest: {z} − {10} = {z - 10}.

cards.idea: Electrons fill shells in order: up to {2}, then up to {8}, then up to {8}.
A Bohr diagram shows the nucleus and each shell with its electrons.
The outer shell is the last shell; its electrons decide how the element reacts.

check.prompt: How many electrons are in the outer shell of {nameOf(s)} (atomic number {atomicNumber(s)})?

misconceptions.explain: That is the number of shells; count the electrons in the last one.

solution: The last number is the outer shell: {answer}.

questions.prompt: What is the electron arrangement of {nameOf(s)} (atomic number {atomicNumber(s)})?

misconceptions.explain: The first shell holds 2 electrons when the atom has more than 2.

solution: {atomicNumber(s)} electrons: up to {2} in the first shell, up to {8} in the next, then up to {8}.

questions.prompt: This Bohr model shows an atom. How many electrons does it have?
solution: Count the dots on every shell: {shells(z)}.

questions.prompt: How many electrons are in the outer shell of {nameOf(s)} (atomic number {atomicNumber(s)})?

misconceptions.explain: That is the number of shells; count the electrons in the last one.

solution: The last number is the outer shell: {answer}.

questions.prompt: An atom has the arrangement {shells(z)}. What is its atomic number?

misconceptions.explain: That is only the outer shell; add all the shells.

solution: Add the electrons in every shell.
The total is {answer}, and protons = electrons.
